Guide

Glossary

Definitions of the terms used in the reports, as DappGo uses them.

Advance-decline ratio
The number of tracked tickers that rose on the day divided by the number that fell. Above 1 means more rose than fell.
Annualized yield
An option premium expressed as a yearly percentage of the strike: premium ÷ strike × 365 ÷ days to expiry. Useful for comparing contracts of similar length; misleading for very short ones.
Assignment
What happens when the buyer of an option exercises it. A put seller who is assigned must buy the shares at the strike; a call seller must sell them.
Benchmark
The index a market is measured against. The US report uses the SPY exchange-traded fund; the Taiwan report uses the TAIEX.
Bollinger Bands
A 20-day moving average with a band two standard deviations above and below it. Price near the lower band is low relative to its own recent range.
Breadth
How widely a market move is shared. DappGo's main breadth figure is the share of tracked tickers priced above their own 20-day moving average.
Cash-secured put
Selling a put while holding enough cash to buy the shares at the strike if assigned.
Composite score
The 0 to 100 score the options report uses to rank contracts on one day, combining yield, distance from the share price, delta and time decay. See the methodology.
Coverage
How many of a report's expected tickers actually have data in that revision.
Covered call
Selling a call against shares already owned.
Days to expiry (DTE)
Calendar days until an option contract expires.
Delta
How much an option's price changes for a one-dollar change in the share price. Its absolute value is also a rough estimate of the chance the option finishes in the money.
Foreign investors, investment trusts, dealers
The three institutional groups whose daily net buying and selling Taiwan's exchange publishes. Investment trusts are domestic fund managers; dealers are securities firms trading their own accounts.
Historical volatility
The annualized standard deviation of a stock's daily returns over a past window, 20 sessions in DappGo's reports.
Implied volatility (IV)
The volatility that makes an option-pricing model match the option's market price. It reflects what the market is paying for uncertainty, not what will happen.
In the money, out of the money
A put is in the money when the share price is below the strike, a call when it is above. Out of the money is the reverse; an option that expires out of the money is worthless.
Lot
In Taiwan, 1,000 shares. Institutional flows are quoted in lots.
MACD
Moving average convergence divergence: the 12-day exponential average minus the 26-day one, compared with its own 9-day average. The difference between the two is the histogram.
Market regime
DappGo's one-word reading of the backdrop (risk-on, risk-off, neutral or mixed), computed from the benchmark's moving averages, its volatility and breadth.
Median move
The middle value of the tracked tickers' one-day changes. Half moved more, half less.
Moving average
The average closing price over the last N sessions. The 20-day average tracks the short-term trend, the 200-day the long-term one.
Payload hash
A fingerprint of a report's data file. Two pages showing the same hash were built from identical data.
Premium
The price of an option, quoted per share. One US equity option contract covers 100 shares.
Probability out of the money
A model estimate of the chance an option expires worthless, which is the outcome an option seller wants.
Profit factor
Total gains divided by total losses across a set of trades. Below 1 means the set lost money overall.
RSI
Relative strength index, here over 14 sessions. It runs from 0 to 100 and compares recent gains with recent losses. At or below 30 is conventionally called oversold, at or above 70 overbought.
Sector dispersion
The standard deviation of sector average moves on the day. Higher means sectors moved less in step.
Session
One trading day on an exchange. Archive pages are filed by session date, not by the date the report was generated.
Stochastic oscillator (KD)
An indicator that places the close within its recent high-low range. %K is the fast line and %D its average; %K crossing above %D is read as momentum turning up.
Strike
The price at which an option's underlying shares are bought or sold if it is exercised.
Theta
How much value an option loses per day from the passage of time, all else equal.
Underlying
The stock or ETF an option contract refers to.
Universe
The fixed list of tickers a report tracks.
Win rate
The share of trades in a set that made money. It says nothing about the size of the wins and losses; read it with the profit factor.
52-week position
Where the price sits between its 52-week low (0%) and high (100%).
